stem: In which structure is glycogen found?
rationale: The surplus is stored as glycogen (liver and muscle) or as triacylglycerol in adipose tissue.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: In which structure is triacylglycerol found?
rationale: The surplus is stored as glycogen (liver and muscle) or as triacylglycerol in adipose tissue.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which substance is secreted by the liver?
rationale: After an overnight fast, the liver is the main source of glucose, producing approximately 9 grams per hour in humans (Figure 14-1).
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance is transported by the liver?
rationale: Over 60% of the glucose released by the liver, approximately 6 grams per hour, is metabolized by the central nervous system. Over 60% of the glucose released by the liver, approximately 6 grams per hour, is metabolized by red blood cells.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance does the central nervous system require?
rationale: The central nervous system is largely dependent on glucose. Red blood cells are wholly reliant on glucose.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance do erythrocytes require?
rationale: Red blood cells are wholly reliant on glucose. Adipose tissue releases nonesterified fatty acids by hydrolyzing stored triacylglycerol.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance is secreted by adipose tissue?
rationale: Adipose tissue releases nonesterified fatty acids by hydrolyzing stored triacylglycerol. Nonesterified fatty acids serve as the primary oxidizable fuel for many tissues, including the heart, muscle, and liver.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance is synthesized by the liver?
rationale: In the liver, amino acids are substrates for the synthesis of major plasma proteins, such as albumin and fibrinogen.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Which substance is stored in the liver?
rationale: The liver stores the majority of glucose carbon as glycogen in the fed state.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance do peripheral tissues require?
rationale: Dietary glucose not taken up by the liver is utilized by peripheral tissues for oxidation or storage in the fed state.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance is stored in muscle as a form of glucose storage?
rationale: Glucose is stored in muscle as glycogen in the fed state.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Which substance is stored in adipose tissue as a form of glucose storage?
rationale: Glucose is stored in adipose tissue as triacylglycerol in the fed state.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > OVERVIEW OF SUBSTRATE METABOLISM IN FASTING & FEASTING

stem: Lipids are converted into which substances during processing?
rationale: Lipids are processed into fatty acids and glycerol.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET

stem: In ruminants, dietary cellulose is converted into which substances by symbiotic microorganisms?
rationale: In ruminants, dietary cellulose is fermented by symbiotic microorganisms to short-chain fatty acids, including acetic, propionic, and butyric acids.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET

stem: Hexokinase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Glucose is first metabolized to glucose-6-phosphate by hexokinase.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Carbohydrate Metabolism Is Centered on Oxidation & Storage of Glucose

stem: Glucose-6-phosphate is converted into which substance in the glycolytic pathway?
rationale: Glucose-6-phosphate can be metabolized to pyruvate by the pathway of glycolysis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Carbohydrate Metabolism Is Centered on Oxidation & Storage of Glucose

stem: Pyruvate is converted into which substance through carboxylation?
rationale: Pyruvate can be carboxylated to oxaloacetate.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE

stem: Which substance is stored in skeletal muscle as a form of glucose storage?
rationale: Glucose can be stored as a polymer called glycogen in skeletal muscle and liver.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Carbohydrate Metabolism Is Centered on Oxidation & Storage of Glucose

stem: Glucose is converted into which substance?
rationale: Glucose can be diverted to the pentose phosphate pathway.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Carbohydrate Metabolism Is Centered on Oxidation & Storage of Glucose

stem: Triose phosphate is converted into which substance in the glycolytic pathway?
rationale: In the glycolytic pathway, triose phosphate intermediates can give rise to the glycerol moiety of triacylglycerols.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Carbohydrate Metabolism Is Centered on Oxidation & Storage of Glucose

stem: What substance is released when triacylglycerol is mobilized in adipose tissue?
rationale: Stored triacylglycerol in adipose tissue can be mobilized through lipolysis to release nonesterified fatty acids and glycerol.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Lipid Metabolism Is Concerned Mainly With Fatty Acids & Cholesterol

stem: What substance is formed from acetoacetate through nonenzymatic decarboxylation?
rationale: The ketone bodies are acetoacetate, 3-hydroxybutyrate, and acetone, with acetone formed nonenzymically by decarboxylation of acetoacetate (Figure 14-3).
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Lipid Metabolism Is Concerned Mainly With Fatty Acids & Cholesterol

stem: Which substance can amino acids be used to synthesize?
rationale: Many of the amino acids, arising from the diet or from tissue protein turnover, can be used for gluconeogenesis, as can the glycerol from triacylglycerol.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels

stem: Carbon skeletons requires which substance?
rationale: The carbon backbone of an amino acid must have the alpha amino nitrogen removed through deamination if it is to be used for other processes.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Much of Amino Acid Metabolism Involves Transamination

stem: Carbon skeletons are converted into which substance?
rationale: Additionally, the carbon skeletons can be used to synthesize fatty acids or form ketone bodies.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > PATHWAYS TO PROCESS THE MAJOR PRODUCTS OF OUR DIET > Much of Amino Acid Metabolism Involves Transamination

stem: Where is glucose absorbed after the digestion of carbohydrates?
rationale: Glucose resulting from the digestion of carbohydrates is absorbed via the hepatic portal vein.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: What substance is nitrogen converted into before being excreted?
rationale: The nitrogen is converted to urea, transported to the kidney, and excreted.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Which substance is secreted by intestinal mucosa?
rationale: Monoacylglycerols and fatty acids are reesterified in the intestinal mucosa and packaged with protein, such as apolipoproteins, and secreted into the lymphatic system as chylomicrons, bypassing the liver.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: What happens to the fatty acids released from chylomicron triacylglycerol by lipoprotein lipase?
rationale: Chylomicron triacylglycerol is first metabolized by tissues that have lipoprotein lipase, which hydrolyzes the triacylglycerol, releasing fatty acids that are incorporated into tissue lipids or oxidized as fuel.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Which substance is synthesised by adipose tissue?
rationale: The other major source of long-chain fatty acids is synthesis from carbohydrate in adipose tissue and the liver through lipogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Which substance is transported by fatty acids?
rationale: Fatty acids are transported bound to serum albumin. Fatty acids are taken up by most tissues.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Which substance is transported by very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL)?
rationale: Very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) is secreted into the circulation. This triacylglycerol undergoes a fate similar to that of chylomicrons. Fatty acids can be partially oxidized in the liver in the fasting setting to form ketone bodies through ketogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: What is a recognized primary fuel for muscle in the fasted state?
rationale: Skeletal muscle's primary fuel is fatty acids in the fasted setting.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Which substance is synthesised by muscle?
rationale: Skeletal muscle synthesizes muscle protein from plasma amino acids.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > METABOLIC PATHWAYS AT THE ORGAN & CELLULAR LEVEL > The Anatomical Location of an Organ & the Blood Circulation Integrates Metabolism

stem: Phenylalanine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, and isoleucine give rise to both acetyl-CoA and intermediates that can be used for gluconeogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE

stem: Tyrosine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, and isoleucine give rise to both acetyl-CoA and intermediates that can be used for gluconeogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE

stem: Tryptophan is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, and isoleucine give rise to both acetyl-CoA and intermediates that can be used for gluconeogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE

stem: Isoleucine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, and isoleucine give rise to both acetyl-CoA and intermediates that can be used for gluconeogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE

stem: Amino acids are mobilized from which structure during prolonged fasting?
rationale: During prolonged fasting and starvation, amino acids are mobilized from muscle protein to provide substrates for gluconeogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE

stem: Which substance is synthesized by the mammary gland during lactation?
rationale: The mammary gland requires glucose for the synthesis of lactose during lactation.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE > Glucose Is Always Required by the Central Nervous System & Erythrocytes

stem: Which substance is primarily oxidized by the heart for energy?
rationale: In tissues such as the heart, metabolic fuels are oxidized in the following order of preference: fatty acids, ketone bodies, and glucose (Figure 14–9).
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE > Glucose Is Always Required by the Central Nervous System & Erythrocytes

stem: What substance are chylomicrons converted into?
rationale: Chylomicrons are the largest plasma lipoproteins.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE > In the Fed State, the Exogenous Metabolic Fuels Are Both Oxidized & Stored

stem: The intestine is part of which anatomical structure?
rationale: In the fasting state, the decrease in glucose concentration in the portal blood from the small intestine leads to a reduction in insulin secretion.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > MANY METABOLIC FUELS ARE INTERCONVERTIBLE > Metabolic Fuel Reserves Are Mobilized in the Fasting State

stem: Acetyl-CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Acetyl-CoA is the precursor for synthesis of long-chain fatty acids, steroids (including cholesterol), and ketone bodies.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of ketosis?
rationale: Due to very low carbohydrate intake and high fat oxidation, a mild ketosis develops. Ketone bodies are provided to the brain to support energy requirements not met by glucose.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of ketoacidosis?
rationale: In ewes carrying twin pregnancies, it can result in pronounced ketoacidosis and profound hypoglycemia. Ketogenic diets are characterized by low carbohydrate intake (<50 g/day).
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of hypoglycemia?
rationale: In ewes carrying twin pregnancies, it can result in pronounced ketoacidosis and profound hypoglycemia. Ketogenic diets are characterized by low carbohydrate intake (<50 g/day).
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Blindness can develop as a complication of which condition?
rationale: Inadequate diabetes management can lead to organ dysfunction, including blindness, renal and cardiovascular diseases.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of type 2 diabetes?
rationale: Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) is due to a combination of insulin resistance and impaired insulin secretion.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Diabetic ketoacidosis can develop as a complication of which condition?
rationale: Severe hyperglycemia can progress to diabetic ketoacidosis, a medical emergency. In the absence of adequate insulin, the actions of glucagon are not antagonized, leading to increased gluconeogenesis.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of coma?
rationale: Coma results from both the acidosis and the increased osmolality of the extracellular fluid and dehydration. Increased osmolality of the extracellular fluid and dehydration are primarily due to hyperglycemia and diuresis from the excretion of glucose and ketone bodies in the urine.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of dehydration?
rationale: Increased osmolality of the extracellular fluid and dehydration are primarily due to hyperglycemia and diuresis from the excretion of glucose and ketone bodies in the urine.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels > CLINICAL ASPECTS

stem: Which substance is transported by lipids?
rationale: Lipids and lipid-soluble products of digestion enter the bloodstream from the lymphatic system, and the liver clears the remnants after extrahepatic tissues have taken up fatty acids.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels

stem: Gluconeogenesis is converted into which substance?
rationale: As the fast progresses, the contribution of gluconeogenesis is the primary source of glucose carbon.
citation: chapter_14_overview_of_metabolism_and_the_provision_of_metabolic_fuels — Overview of Metabolism & the Provision of Metabolic Fuels
